title: Unions and students plan nationwide strike and protests in France

tea.why: Protesters are responding to calls for a national day of mobilization over wages, jobs, public services, industry, and cost of living.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand government responses regarding salaries, employment, public services, and cost-of-living issues.
tea.changed: Nov 4: Intelligence notes classified the upcoming mobilization as high risk, estimating hundreds of thousands of participants and anticipated blockades.

summary: Trade unions, student groups, and yellow vest coordinators have organized a nationwide day of strikes and protests across France, including Paris, scheduled for November 5. According to territorial intelligence reports cited in news sources, between 500,000 and 700,000 demonstrators are anticipated nationwide, alongside expected school and university blockades and numerous union processions. The movement brings together private and public sector employees, retirees, students, and other groups demanding improvements in wages, jobs, public services, and industry, as well as addressing the high cost of living. Rail and public transport networks, educational institutions, and aviation services anticipate disruptions. Authorities have classified the mobilization as high risk, warning of potential public order disturbances.
response: According to news reports, the territorial intelligence service classified the mobilization as high risk due to anticipated violence and property damage. The Education Ministry estimated a 17.54% strike rate in the primary public sector.

updates.text: Territorial intelligence reports estimated between 500,000 and 700,000 protesters would participate nationwide outside the Paris region.
Rail and transport operators announced anticipated traffic disruptions ahead of the nationwide strike called by trade unions.
